defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: netrc_auth.py:17 expanduser(f"~/{name}") prepends ~/ to absolute NETRC path, file never found, credentials lost
netrc_auth.py:12 empty NETRC string accepted, resolves to home dir, netrc raises and returns None
netrc_auth.py:17 tilde-prefixed NETRC (~/my_netrc) becomes ~/~/my_netrc, file not found
test only covers relative NETRC name, not absolute path
votes.evidence_quote: `os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}")` always prepends `~/` to the NETRC value. When the user sets `NETRC=/etc/secrets/netrc` (the convention followed by git, curl, wget), `name` is `/etc/secrets/netrc`, so the expression produces `~/etc/secrets/netrc` → `$HOME/etc/secrets/netrc`. The file is never found, credentials are silently lost.
votes.justification: The review identifies the expanduser call at line 17 in get_netrc_auth. It explains that an absolute NETRC path ends up under the home directory, so the file is never found and no credentials are returned, which is the known defect. A separate item covers the tilde-prefixed case, which is part of the same defect.
